class.name: SQLiteColumn
class.brief_description: A column of a table in an [SQLiteDatabase].

members.member: The type SQLite prefers for values in this column, derived from [member declared_type] by SQLite's rules: a type that contains [code]INT[/code] is [constant AFFINITY_INTEGER]; else one with [code]CHAR[/code], [code]CLOB[/code] or [code]TEXT[/code] is [constant AFFINITY_TEXT]; else one with [code]BLOB[/code], or no type, is [constant AFFINITY_BLOB]; else one with [code]REAL[/code], [code]FLOAT[/code] or [code]DOUBLE[/code] (the first four letters are enough) is [constant AFFINITY_REAL]; everything else is [constant AFFINITY_NUMERIC]. [b]Note:[/b] Except in [code]STRICT[/code] tables, a column can still hold values of any type.
The type as written in [code]CREATE TABLE[/code], for example [code]VARCHAR(40)[/code]. Empty if the column was declared without a type.
The SQL text of the [code]DEFAULT[/code] expression, for example [code]'none'[/code] (with quotes), [code]0[/code] or [code]CURRENT_TIMESTAMP[/code]. Empty if the column has no default.
If [code]true[/code], the column has a [code]NOT NULL[/code] constraint.

The position of the column in the primary key, starting at [code]1[/code]. [code]0[/code] if the column is not part of the primary key. For [code]PRIMARY KEY (b, a)[/code], [code]b[/code] is [code]1[/code] and [code]a[/code] is [code]2[/code].

constants.constant: The column stores values as they are ([code]BLOB[/code], or no declared type).
The column prefers numbers but keeps text that is not a number ([code]NUMERIC[/code], [code]DECIMAL[/code], [code]BOOLEAN[/code], [code]DATE[/code], [code]DATETIME[/code], …).
